note_sections.t: Re-evaluation for treatment decision following prior prostate cancer diagnosis and recent PSA rise.

Long-standing referral for prostate cancer management. Patient is a 69-year-old retired logistics manager with a history of type 2 diabetes, hypercholesterolaemia, and osteoarthritis. He is married and lives in an assisted-living facility. PSA trend shows progressive rise from 2.3 ng/mL in Jan 2023 to 7.0 ng/mL in Jan 2025. He reports moderate LUTS with IPSS 15/35. He smokes 17 pack-years and swims once weekly. Recent ophthalmology review for cataracts and quarterly diabetes nurse follow-up are noted. No bone pain or haematuria.
On DRE, the prostate is smooth and symmetric with no palpable nodules, consistent with cT1c. General examination shows stable vitals with BP 147/79 mmHg and HR 85 bpm. No lymphadenopathy or edema.
